summary: Early integration discovery for Cobalt Dynamics evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main focus: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer sensitive to data residency and wants benchmark before committing to Dedicated.
transcript: [00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE for the Cobalt account. Priya from our SE team is on as well.
[00:08] Alex (Cobalt CTO): Hey, thanks. Alex here. Maya and Evan are on too. Appreciate the time.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick agenda: integration patterns, SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy questions, rate limiting, and observability hooks. Sound good?

[00:20] Maya (Cobalt): Yep. We're most interested in how Redwood fits into our existing stack — we use a Kong gateway, OpenTelemetry for traces, and a LangChain-based retrieval pipeline for customer support use cases.
[00:28] Evan (Backend Lead): Also want to understand Dedicated vs Hosted from an ops/cost perspective — and private deployment options for sensitive PII workloads.
[00:35] Jordan: Great. Quick clarification: when you say LangChain pipeline, is that primarily the Retriever + Chat chain for RAG, or a custom orchestration?

[00:42] Maya: Mostly Retriever + Summarize + Chat. We're using LlamaIndex for some ingestion as well — it's a mix. We want to keep the current code but swap out the model endpoint for Redwood, ideally via SDK or an HTTP gateway.

[00:50] Priya: Perfect — Redwood's SDKs have connectors/examples for both LangChain and LlamaIndex. They include retriever wrappers and an adapter that implements the LangChain LLM interface so it's a pretty thin swap. There's also a plain HTTP gateway proxy path if you prefer to route through Kong.
[01:05] Alex: How thin is "thin" — will we need to refactor prompts or change tokenization logic?

[01:09] Priya: Not generally. The SDK returns the same text payloads. You might need small prompt work for system prompts or stop tokens, but tokenization is model-specific — if you use a different model family you'd test. Our LangChain adapter exposes the same call signatures, so minimal code changes.
[01:22] Evan: If we go through Kong gateway, are there special headers or auth we need to add? We prefer not to expose API keys wider than necessary.

[01:28] Jordan: You can put Redwood behind your gateway and handle auth at the gateway level by using a per-service proxy key. We support short-lived tokens, and for Dedicated/Private you can also integrate SSO and mTLS.
[01:36] Maya: For the private deployment, is the control plane still hosted? We need to know where logs and usage metrics live.

[01:40] Priya: Good question. For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), the control plane can be customer-hosted in your VPC; logs and traces can be forwarded to your collectors. In Dedicated we support customer-specific logging destinations and KMS integration so keys never leave your KMS.
[01:52] Alex: Cool. On rate limits — our traffic pattern is spiky: baseline 20 rps, spikes to 120 rps for short bursts. How do Redwood quotas and burst policies work?

[02:00] Priya: Hosted has per-account rate limits and per-route quotas; we do token-based rate limiting and can configure burst windows. Dedicated offers reserved capacity with predictable throughput and you can configure burst pools. We can run capacity planning to map your QPS to GPU instance types and batching settings.
[02:12] Evan: Does batching increase latency for short requests? Our chat flow needs sub-200ms sometimes.

[02:16] Priya: There's a tradeoff — continuous batching improves throughput and cost, but we have latency-aware routing: low-latency SLOs route to prewarmed instances with smaller batch windows. For sub-200ms you'd want a Dedicated pool tuned for low latency or the hosted low-latency tier for critical traffic.
[02:28] Maya: How does observability look — we use Datadog and OpenTelemetry. Can Redwood emit traces/span IDs so we can correlate end-to-end?

[02:35] Jordan: Yes, we provide request-level correlation IDs in headers and support OpenTelemetry export. You can forward traces to your APM, and our Console has model-level breakdowns for latency, token cost, and errors. We also provide webhooks for real-time metrics.
[02:47] Alex: Is there a sample integration for Datadog/OTel? We need to show security that we aren't losing visibility.

[02:51] Priya: We'll share a repo with examples: Datadog dashboards, an OTel instrumentation example, and our SDK hooks that emit spans. Also sample nginx/Kong config for proxying and adding auth headers.
[02:59] Evan: On security, do you support KMS for key wrapping and customer-managed keys?
[03:03] Priya: Yes — Dedicated and Private support KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options). For Hosted we use our KMS but we can discuss Bring Your Own Key in some enterprise plans.
[03:12] Maya: We run some PII pipelines; could we keep those on Private and send lower-sensitivity workloads to Hosted?

[03:16] Jordan: That's a common pattern. Smart routing policies let you route requests by tag, tenant, or SLA to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. You can also have automatic fallback to a cheaper model family if capacity is constrained.
[03:27] Alex: About models — are you hosting our own fine-tuned models or using open weights?
[03:31] Priya: Both options. Customers can bring their own model artifacts to Dedicated/Private or use our curated open models. We handle quantization/compilation and kernel selection in the runtime.
[03:40] Maya: We currently use a fine-tuned Llama variant. How does that map into Redwood's SDK? Any special steps for KV cache or past conversation context?

[03:47] Priya: The SDK supports KV cache handling for autoregressive models; we expose hooks to snapshot and reuse KV caches. For chat history we recommend prefix caching and our SDK includes utilities to manage context windows efficiently.
[03:58] Evan: Any guidance on token limits and rolling windows? We have long-doc summarization jobs too.

[04:02] Jordan: We'll share best-practices: chunking docs, using embeddings retrievers (LangChain/LlamaIndex), and configuring quantization for long context models. For very long contexts you can use our streaming responses with incremental decoding.
[04:12] Maya: Can the SDK be used from our python microservices? Or do you have a Go client? We have services in both.
[04:16] Priya: We have SDKs for Python, Node, and Go, plus a simple HTTP API. LangChain and LlamaIndex examples are Python-first, but the HTTP adapter works from any language.
[04:25] Alex: About cost — can you give a rough comparison Hosted vs Dedicated for our expected load? We care about unit cost per token and fixed monthly overhead.

[04:32] Priya: We'll run an analysis. Hosted is usage-based with per-token pricing; Dedicated is committed capacity — higher fixed cost but lower marginal token price. Given your spiky pattern, a hybrid approach (Dedicated for baseline + Hosted for bursts) often wins on cost and reliability.
[04:44] Evan: Any pitfalls when connecting via Kong? We want to preserve client IPs for rate limiting and per-tenant quotas.

[04:49] Jordan: You can forward original IPs in headers; our gateway supports X-Forwarded-For. For per-tenant quotas you can set route-based rate limits and attach tokens per tenant. We also support per-route quotas and usage tagging for billing.
[04:59] Maya: Do you expose token-level cost breakdowns in the Console? We need to show product teams where costs are coming from.
[05:03] Jordan: Yes — per-request and per-route cost, token breakdowns, and per-model dashboards. You can also export raw usage to S3/BigQuery for custom analysis.
[05:11] Alex: For the benchmark we want: latency p50/p95 for our typical chat prompt, and throughput for batch summarization. Can Redwood run that or do we need to run locally?

[05:18] Priya: We can run initial bench estimates and provide a recommended Dedicated sizing. For customer-specific payloads we recommend running a quick on-prem or dedicated benchmark — we can help provision a pilot Dedicated node or run a hosted benchmark with your sample prompts.
[05:29] Evan: What's the onboarding time for a Dedicated pool?

[05:32] Jordan: Typically 2–4 weeks for initial provisioning and testing, faster if you accept standard instance types. Private on-prem installs can be longer depending on network and compliance requirements.
[05:40] Maya: We will need SOC2 docs and a data processing addendum for legal.
[05:44] Jordan: We'll share the SOC2 pack and DPA link after this call.
[05:47] Alex: Any known gotchas with LlamaIndex connectors? We had one issue with embeddings mismatching between local and cloud.

[05:53] Priya: Embedding dimension mismatches often come from different model families or tokenizers. Our LangChain/LlamaIndex examples include embedding spec and a verification script to validate dims and distances.
[06:03] Maya: For observability hooks, does Redwood provide a webhook that can push per-request metrics to our stream? We want near-real-time alerts on error spikes.
[06:08] Jordan: Yes — webhooks for request-level metrics and a streaming telemetry API. You can also stream a filtered set of traces and events to your ingestion pipeline.
[06:15] Evan: If we do a proxy route through Kong, and Kong handles auth, can we do additional per-tenant headers for model selection? e.g., tenant-model: small-vs-large?
[06:22] Priya: Absolutely — routing keys can be header-based. You can set up policies to pick model variants or quality tiers and we support automatic fallback rules.
[06:29] Alex: OK, let's recap next steps.

[06:31] Jordan: Recap: we'll send integration guide, SDK samples for LangChain/LlamaIndex, Datadog/OTel examples, and SOC2 pack. Priya will scope Dedicated sizing and a benchmark plan. Alex will share gateway config and sample prompts/datasets.
[06:43] Maya: Sounds good. Timeline: we'd like the bench results before end of year if possible.
[06:47] Jordan: We'll try to hit that — Jordan to send artifacts by 2026-12-23; Priya to propose sizing by 2026-12-28; schedule bench for week of 2026-12-27.
[06:56] Alex: Great, thanks everyone.
[06:58] Jordan: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:00] (meeting ends)
